ships.name: Bob Cook (1907)
ships.story: The scow Bob Cook foundered somewhere between Superior, Wisconsin and Bayfield, Wisconsin in November of 1937.

ships.name: Clarence (1930)
ships.cargo: Built as a fish tug, converted to a bumboat (harbor supply boat). She had $3,500 worth of supplies on board.
ships.story: Clarence burned and exploded at Superior, Wisconsin on June 30, 1938 after filling her 150-gallon gasoline tank. A short in the starting motor was thought to have caused the blaze, which destroyed the vessel.

ships.name: Commodore Jack Barry (1885)
ships.cargo: None at the time of the fire.

ships.name: Herring King
ships.cargo: Loaded with a good load of fish from the Moe Fishery on Sand Island.
ships.story: Hull towed to Sand Island and used as a cabin base

ships.name: Ira H. Owen (1887)
ships.cargo: 116,000 bushels of barley which was a light load.
ships.story: No recorded search. 19 lost in the 1905 Mataafa storm; wreckage seen 12 miles east of Michigan Island

ships.name: John A. Paige (1881)
ships.cargo: Had been in the process of building a log raft for towing.
ships.story: Burned to the waterline in Siskiwit Bay, 1892

ships.name: Manistee (1867)
ships.cargo: 10,000 bushels of oats, 90 tons of mill feed, 1,254 barrels of flour, 9 tons of furniture and merchandise, a large quant
ships.story: Sheltered at Bayfield for 4 days, left on the 5th and vanished with all aboard

ships.name: May Corgan (1883?)
ships.story: Lost off Bark Point when the tow line parted in a gale; probably scattered in about 30 ft

ships.name: Ozaukee (1861)
ships.cargo: Supplies for south shore fishermen and Montreal River miners.
ships.story: On may 26, 1884 the sidewheel steamer tug Ozaukee loaded supplies for south shore fishermen and Montreal River miners and headed out facing a stiff breeze.

ships.name: Prussia (1873)
ships.story: Burned off Sand Island; the light keeper saved all 11 crew

ships.name: T.H. Camp (1876)
ships.cargo: Load of camp supplies for W.T. Gardner & Company's lumber camp at the head of Madeline Island.
ships.story: The T.H.Camp simply foundered enroute from Ashland via Bayfield to the northern tip of Madeline Island while carrying a deck load estimated at nearly 20 tons of supplies for the W.T. Gardner lumber camp.

ships.name: Cormorant (1873)
ships.story: Burned off Basswood Island; the hull may have been towed away and salvaged
